skill.name: file-path-traversal-testing
skill.description: Guides authorized security teams through path traversal assessment, verification, impact analysis, and remediation for web applications.
skill.summary: Authorized web application path traversal testing and remediation guidance.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most non-format findings are confirmed: the skill provides a step-by-step path traversal exploitation playbook for sensitive file disclosure and LFI-to-RCE. Markdown backtick matches and two safety or limitation lines were dismissed as false positives. Publication should be blocked unless the content is rewritten as tightly scoped defensive guidance with safe lab-only examples.

remediation.suggestion: Rewrite the skill around authorized defensive assessment, safe test fixtures, and clear stop conditions instead of arbitrary file extraction.
Remove references to SSH private keys, password files, SAM hives, and real configuration secrets. Use benign canary files in controlled labs.
Remove PHP system(), log poisoning, php://input, data://, and expect:// command execution examples. Replace them with non-executing risk explanations.
Add authorization checks, rate limits, scope constraints, and guidance to use local training applications or approved staging targets only.

content.value_statement: Path traversal flaws expose sensitive server files when input builds file paths. This skill outlines discovery, verification, impact analysis, and remediation for authorized web security testing.
actual_capabilities: Identifies file-related parameters and application features that may build filesystem paths.
Explains common traversal payload forms, encodings, and bypass patterns for authorized testing.
Describes manual and automated testing workflows with browser tools, Burp Suite, ffuf, and wfuzz.
Lists Linux, Windows, web server, and application file classes often used for impact assessment.
Connects verified findings to remediation patterns such as allowlists and canonical path checks.
Explains escalation paths from local file inclusion to command execution for risk evaluation.
limitations: Testing must stay inside written authorization and approved target scope.
It cannot bypass operating system permissions when the application user lacks file access.
Examples may be blocked by validation, web application firewalls, or framework routing.
Several payloads are unsafe outside a lab or controlled penetration test.

use_cases.title: Validate a Web Download Endpoint
use_cases.description: Check whether a file download or document viewer can escape its intended storage directory.

use_cases.title: Review File Handling Fixes
use_cases.description: Compare remediation code against safe path canonicalization, allowlist, and base directory checks.

use_cases.title: Prepare an AppSec Finding
use_cases.description: Organize evidence, impact, affected parameters, and remediation guidance for an authorized assessment report.

prompt_templates.title: Map File Inputs
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner reconnaissance for an authorized target.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these routes and parameters for file-handling behavior. Identify likely path traversal test points and explain why each matters.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Safe Verification
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate testing without accessing sensitive production data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a path traversal verification plan for this authorized endpoint. Use harmless canary files and include clear stop conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Impact
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced triage after a confirmed traversal issue.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help assess the impact of this confirmed path traversal flaw. Separate safe evidence from sensitive data that should not be collected.

prompt_templates.title: Design Remediation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this file access design and propose remediation for traversal risk. Include validation, canonicalization, logging, and regression tests.

output_examples.input: A download endpoint accepts a filename parameter and returns different errors for missing files.
output_examples.output: The output ranks the parameter as high priority, suggests safe canary-file checks, lists evidence to capture, and recommends base-directory validation.

output_examples.input: A developer shares a proposed fix that strips parent directory sequences from the requested filename.
output_examples.output: The output explains why stripping is fragile, recommends allowlisted identifiers, canonical path comparison, and regression tests for encoded variants.

output_examples.input: An assessment needs a concise finding for a verified traversal issue.
output_examples.output: The output provides a professional finding summary, impact statement, reproduction boundaries, affected endpoint notes, and remediation guidance.

best_practices: Use written authorization, defined scope, and harmless proof files before any testing begins.
Prefer allowlisted file identifiers over user-supplied paths in application design.
Record minimal evidence and avoid collecting real secrets or private user data.
anti_patterns: Testing public systems without permission or a defined engagement scope.
Using production secrets, password files, or private keys as proof of impact.
Relying on string replacement filters instead of canonical path validation.

faq.question: What is path traversal?
faq.answer: Path traversal is a flaw where user input lets an application access files outside the intended directory.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: It is intended for security teams, developers, and reviewers working on authorized web application assessments.

faq.question: Does it execute tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides methodology and example workflows that a human must adapt to an approved scope.

faq.question: Can it prove impact without sensitive files?
faq.answer: Yes. Use canary files, controlled test fixtures, or non-sensitive files created for the assessment.

faq.question: What fixes does it recommend?
faq.answer: It recommends allowlists, canonical path checks, strict base directories, and tests for encoded traversal variants.

faq.question: Why is this skill high risk?
faq.answer: It includes payloads and workflows that can disclose sensitive files or support command execution on vulnerable systems.
